title: Coherence from a single formal quotient and an annihilated map kernel
statement: Let X be affine Noetherian, J ideal sheaf data, F a quasi-coherent module, H coherent, and a:F -> H [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let s>=1. If the quotient of F by J^s F (the formal completion component at index s-1) is coherent and J^s annihilates kernel(a), then F is coherent. No cokernel bound or other formal quotient condition is needed.

source.place: Tag 0889(1), finiteness paragraph; elementary finite-generator argument replacing the use of Tag 05EU

proof.text: Let U be the top affine open and A its Noetherian ring of sections. Put I=J(U)^s. Quasi-coherence of the kernel and the affine ideal-power vanishing criterion show that I kills the kernel of the linear map a on sections.

Reuse Scheme.Modules.multiplication_range from IdealTimesQuasiCoherentAffineSections (a proof-only import all exposes its private theorem), rather than proving the multiplication-range calculation again. The ideal-power section comparison identifies its ideal with I=J(U)^s. Use the tensor and image comparisons for quasi-coherence of the product, and the affine cokernel comparison to identify sections of F/J^s F with P/IP. The formal quotient at index s-1 is exactly this cokernel because s>=1. Its assumed coherence makes P/IP finite; coherence of H makes Gamma(H) finite.

The image of P -> Gamma(H) is finite over Noetherian A. Choose a finite submodule L1 of P mapping onto it by lifting a finite generating family. Choose a finite submodule L2 mapping onto P/IP in the same way, and set L=L1+L2. For r in I and x in P, choose y in L1 with a(y)=a(x); I kills x-y, so rx=ry belongs to L. Thus IP is contained in L. Since L2 maps onto P/IP, IP+L2=P. Therefore L=P, proving finite generation. This argument is implemented by proved private helpers exists_fg_lift and finite_of_quotient_and_torsion_kernel.

The affine finite-type criterion gives finite type of F from its finite sections on the singleton cover by U. Combine quasi-coherence with finite type on the Noetherian scheme to obtain coherence. For I=0 the quotient already is P; for I=A the kernel is zero and P embeds in a finite module. The empty spectrum presents no exception.

mathlib_searches.query: A quasi coherent module on an affine Noetherian scheme is coherent if its formal quotients are coherent and it maps to a coherent module with kernel killed by a power of an ideal
A module mapping to a finite module whose kernel is annihilated by an ideal is finite if its quotient by that ideal is finite

theorem coherent_of_formalQuotients_and_torsionKernel
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (H : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ H.obj)
    (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    (hquot : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace
      (((formalCompletionFunctor J).obj F).obj (op (s - 1))))
    (hker : IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
      (kernel a))) :
    RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F
